chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim and Yusuf ibn 'Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
“If the slave of the Imam takes, his hand is not cut. But if one of my slaves steals from the property of the governorship, I would cut off his hand.”
And he said: I heard him saying, “If a slave or a hired worker steals from the property of his master/employer, then there is no amputation upon him.”

key_terms.رَقِيقُ: a slave or bondsman under ownership
key_terms.قَطَعْتُ يَدَهُ: I would cut off his hand; meaning the hadd punishment of theft
key_terms.قَطْعٌ: amputation as the prescribed hadd punishment
key_terms.مَالِ اَلْإِمَارَةِ: the property of the governorship or public authority

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd of theft applied to a slave or hired worker who steals from the property of his owner or from public funds?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings regarding theft by those who are attached to an owner or authority, such as a slave or hired worker. It distinguishes between theft from a private owner’s property and theft from public or governmental property, indicating differing legal consequences in the application of the hadd.
